title: Affine-group scalar-extended dual-number calculus data and compatibility
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ for its existing identity tangent module and $\mathrm df$ for the differential of a homomorphism [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation, def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. For a commutative $k$-algebra $R$, write $R[\delta]$ for the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers], $p_R:R[\delta]\to R$ for $\delta\mapsto0$, and
$$\operatorname{Kernel}_G(R)=\{x\in G(R[\delta]):G(p_R)(x)=1\}.$$
For $h:R\to S$ over $k$, put $\operatorname{dualMap}(h)(r+\delta s)=h(r)+\delta h(s)$; $\operatorname{reduction}(R)=p_R$.

A dual-number calculus datum $D$ on $G$ consists of the following data and conditions. Its tangent module $\mathfrak g$ is finite-dimensional, and for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ it supplies a bijection
$$E_{G,R}:R\otimes_k\mathfrak g\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Kernel}_G(R),$$
using the tensor product and scalar extension [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change]. It satisfies $E_R(v+w)=E_R(v)E_R(w)$, $E_R(0)=1$, $E_R(-v)=E_R(v)^{-1}$, and $G(\delta\mapsto a\delta)E_R(v)=E_R(av)$ for every $a\in R$. At $R=k$, $E_k(1\otimes v)$ is the actual tangent point of $v$. It is natural in $h:R\to S$: applying $G(\operatorname{dualMap}(h))$ to $E_R(v)$ gives $E_S((h\otimes\mathrm{id})v)$.

It also supplies homomorphisms $\operatorname{Ad}_R:G(R)\to\operatorname{GL}_R(R\otimes_k\mathfrak g)$ characterized by
$$j_{R[\delta]}E_R(v)j_{R[\delta]}^{-1}=E_R(\operatorname{Ad}_R(j)v).$$
For every $n\geq0$ and basis $b$ of $\mathfrak g$ indexed by $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, there is a unique group-scheme homomorphism $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ whose value on each $R$-point, interpreted as an $R$-linear automorphism via the base-changed basis $b_R$, is $\operatorname{Ad}_R$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. The case $n=0$ uses the empty matrix group.

For two such data $D$ on $G$ and $D'$ on $H$ and a group-scheme homomorphism $f:G\to H$, the proposition $\operatorname{Compatible}(D,D',f)$ has three clauses. First, for every $R$ and $v\in R\otimes_k\mathfrak g$,
$$f(E_{G,R}(v))=E_{H,R}((\mathrm df)_R(v)).$$
Second, if $f$ is a closed subgroup inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion], its differential is injective and for every $R$,
$$\{E_{H,R}((\mathrm df)_R(v)):v\in R\otimes_k\mathfrak g\}=f(G(R[\delta]))\cap\operatorname{Kernel}_H(R).$$
Third, for every $R$, $j\in G(R)$ and $v\in R\otimes_k\mathfrak g$,
$$(\mathrm df)_R(\operatorname{Ad}_{G,R}(j)v)=\operatorname{Ad}_{H,R}(f(j))((\mathrm df)_R(v)).$$
All test algebras are allowed, including nonreduced and zero algebras. These are the definitions of the datum and its compatibility, not an assertion that such data exist.
